task.name: Sprint cost analytics: post-sprint batchability report
task.story_text:
## What

After a sprint completes, generate an analytics report showing which completed stories would have qualified for cost-aware batching, their actual costs, and whether batching would have been cheaper.

## Why

Before building batch groups as a scheduling feature, we need data on whether batching would actually save money. The v0.7.0 bug-fix sprint is the first large run of small independent stories — the ideal trial. Rather than building the feature on vibes, measure the opportunity first.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Post-sprint report identifies stories that would have qualified for batching (small, independent, implementation_ready, no conflicts, no retries)
- Report shows per-story cost breakdown: preflight, plan (if any), dev, validate, review
- Report groups batch candidates and shows combined cost vs hypothetical batched cost (estimated)
- Report notes which stories conflicted, retried, or escalated (disqualifying them from batches)
- Report shows files touched per story to validate independence assumption
- Output format is human-readable (terminal) with optional YAML/JSON for further analysis

## Notes

This is an experiment/measurement story, not a feature story. Its output should inform the defaults and gating criteria for the batch groups feature. The goal is a decision surface, not a shipping feature.

handoff.summary: Added a post-sprint batchability analytics report. A new pure module (src/theforge/sprint/batch_report.py) reads sprint-summary.yaml, per-story audit.yaml and preflight.yaml, and the optional sprint-rca.yaml, then derives per-story batch eligibility, disqualification reasons, per-phase cost breakdown, touched files, and hypothetical batch groups with measured-vs-estimated cost. Eligibility reuses collision.BATCH_WORK_TYPES (lazy import, since collision pulls in the coordinator engine) and mirrors build_batch_hint's preflight gates, adding post-sprint gates only hindsight affords: non-DONE outcome, dependency edge, conflict, retry, escalation. The batched-cost model — the piece the spec left underspecified — preserves summed per-story preflight cost and charges each shared downstream phase at the max measured member cost; it is labelled an ESTIMATE in the terminal output, the structured payload, and the docs, with an explicit METHODOLOGY statement of what it assumes away. Terminal and YAML/JSON renderers both derive from one BatchabilityReport object so the views cannot drift. A thin CLI command (forge batch-report <run-id>, --format terminal|yaml|json, plus --max-stories/--max-complexity-budget/--max-touched-files sensitivity knobs) is registered in cli/main.py and limited to config resolution, calling the module, printing, and returning explicit nonzero failures for missing/unreadable sprint data.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Post-sprint report identifies stories that would have qualified for batching (small, independent, implementation_ready, no conflicts, no retries)
acceptance_criteria.notes: build_batch_report classifies every story; report.qualified holds stories passing all preflight gates (small / bug-or-mechanical / implementation_ready / known bounded footprint) and all post-sprint gates (DONE outcome, no dependency edge, no conflict, no retry, no escalation). Independence is enforced at grouping time via non-overlapping likely_files. Covered by test_small_independent_ready_stories_qualify and the per-gate disqualification tests.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Report shows per-story cost breakdown: preflight, plan (if any), dev, validate, review
acceptance_criteria.notes: phase_costs covers preflight, plan, plan_review, dev, validate, review (plan_review added for transparency beyond the AC's five). A missing audit phase block renders as $0/— (phase never ran); a block with a null cost_usd stays None and renders '?' with a '+' lower-bound marker on the total, so unmeasured spend is never shown as free (#1992). Rendered as the PER-STORY PHASE COSTS table and as phase_costs_usd in the payload.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Report groups batch candidates and shows combined cost vs hypothetical batched cost (estimated)
acceptance_criteria.notes: Greedy grouping mirrors collision.compute_batch_groups (deterministic issue/slug order, pairwise non-overlapping footprints, combined footprint and complexity ceilings, max_stories cap, groups of one discarded). Each group reports actual_combined_cost_usd, hypothetical_batched_cost_usd, estimated_savings_usd, cheaper_if_batched, and cost_complete. Verified numerically in test_group_reports_actual_and_estimated_cost.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Report notes which stories conflicted, retried, or escalated (disqualifying them from batches)
acceptance_criteria.notes: Each story carries explicit conflicted/retried/escalated booleans plus human-readable disqualifier strings. Conflict = merge-failure outcome or a conflict-mentioning error string; retry = >1 dev iteration or >1 review cycle; escalation = ESCALATE/ESCALATED outcome or an audit escalation block. RCA primary_failure_class enriches disqualified rows when a matching artifact exists. Covered by four dedicated tests.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Report shows files touched per story to validate independence assumption
acceptance_criteria.notes: files_touched is the union of iterations.dev_loop[].files_changed and is rendered for both qualified stories (as 'touched:' beneath the 'predicted:' likely_files line, so prediction and reality sit side by side) and disqualified ones. Group rows additionally render the combined predicted footprint.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Output format is human-readable (terminal) with optional YAML/JSON for further analysis
acceptance_criteria.notes: render_terminal() produces the sectioned terminal report; report_payload() produces a schema-versioned dict that the CLI emits as YAML or JSON. Both read the same BatchabilityReport. Payload round-trip through yaml.safe_dump and json.dumps is asserted in test_payload_matches_report; CLI tests cover all three formats.

story_deviations: The spec's Notes call this an experiment, not a shipping feature; I still wired it as a registered CLI command (forge batch-report) with a docs/guides/cli-reference.md entry, since a decision surface an operator cannot run is not a decision surface. Nothing in the scheduling path changed — the module is read-only over artifacts.

Analysis parameters (max_stories=3, max_complexity_budget=3, max_touched_files=6) are deliberately NOT read from the project's sprint.batch config. Batching is off by default (max_stories=1), so inheriting it would make the report answer 'no opportunity' for every sprint — the exact question it exists to measure. The knobs are exposed as CLI flags for sensitivity analysis and echoed into the payload as batch_rules.

The live independence predicate also consults an 'area:' label parsed from story_text, which is not recoverable from sprint artifacts. Post-sprint independence therefore rests on file footprints alone; this is documented in _compute_groups.

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 fixes the single P1: dependency exclusion was one-sided. The report checked only a story's own depends_on, so a parent story that a sibling depended on had an empty list, passed every gate, and could be placed in a hypothetical batch group — contradicting collision.compute_batch_groups, which excludes BOTH endpoints of a dependency edge because a batch is dispatched as one unit and only the group leader lands a branch. Added _dependents_by_slug(), which reverses the sprint's depends_on edges once before any story report is built, and threaded the result through _build_story_report into _disqualifiers so the parent endpoint is disqualified with its own distinct reason ('dependency edge (depended on by: X)') alongside the existing child-side reason. Added a `dependents` field to StoryBatchReport and to the structured payload so the exclusion is auditable — the parent side is invisible on the story's own summary row, so without it an operator could not tell why a small, clean, implementation-ready story was excluded. Also extracted the ad-hoc depends_on parsing into a _slug_tuple helper used on both sides of the edge map, so keys and values normalise identically and a stray-whitespace entry cannot silently fail to match. Pattern sweep: _compute_groups only consumes eligible stories so it inherits the fix; collision_deps is never persisted to sprint-summary.yaml (verified against sprint/audit.py and sprint/state_writer.py), which is documented on _dependents_by_slug along with why it leaks no bad candidate — a synthetically-serialized story overlaps on likely_files by construction and the grouping step's non-overlap predicate already rejects it.

review_findings_addressed.notes: Sprint-wide reverse edge map (_dependents_by_slug) computed from all summary rows and fed into story disqualification, exactly as the suggested fix described. Both endpoints now carry a distinct, human-readable dependency reason.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.
